🇲🇽🏭 <u>Tariffs or Not, Coahuila's Auto Parts Output Grew 13%</u>

According to the National Auto Parts Industry (INA), Coahuila's auto parts production grew 13% in the first half of 2026, against a national average of 9%. Mexico's auto parts industry produced $63.8 billion in the half, and Coahuila alone made $10.1 billion, about 16 of every 100 dollars. "Our production volumes have been better than expected; that has generated investments equivalent to 1.3 billion dollars," said Lourdes Cobos of the Coahuila Automotive Cluster, as reported by El Economista.

🇲🇽🌴 <u>Acapulco Just Had Its Best Summer in Three Years</u>

Between June and August, Acapulco received 1,609,125 visitors. That is 14.3% more than the 1.41 million of summer 2025 and 24.7% more than in 2024. From January to August, hotel stays reached 4.7 million, up 21.9% year on year, and summer hotel occupancy hit 85.1%, with the Golden Zone at 95.3%. The port that was written off after Hurricane Otis in 2023 is now filling its hotels again.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Veracruz Takes the Biometric CURP From 6 Municipalities to 52 Service Points</u>

Governor Rocío Nahle announced an investment of more than 50 million pesos to expand biometric CURP registration across Veracruz. Right now, the equipment sits in only 6 of the state's 212 municipalities. The new modules will also run as mobile units, so families no longer have to pay to travel to the state capital to get an ID. The state government says the expansion could reach more than 8 million residents.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico Joins a 14-Economy Declaration With Washington on Industrial "Overcapacity"</u>

Mexico and 13 other economies signed a joint ministerial declaration convened by the USTR within the OECD Trade Committee. It targets "structural excess capacity" in five sectors: cars and EVs, batteries, chemicals, foundational semiconductors and solar panels. It blames "non-market policies and practices" of foreign governments. Technical meetings to set the terms of reference start before December 2026. For Mexico, the signature comes in the middle of the T-MEC review and Section 232 talks, with US tariffs on Mexican cars and steel still on the table.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico's Environment Secretary to Congress: "We Are Not Yet in Conditions" for Fracking</u>

Appearing before the Chamber of Deputies' environment and climate committees, Semarnat head Alicia Bárcena said there is no presidential authorization for fracking pilot tests. "No estamos todavía en condiciones de ir adelante con este desarrollo." Before any pilot can happen, Mexico must rewrite its standards and well-construction guidelines. Her conditions: no drinking or farm water, at least 75% water recycling, permanent seismic monitoring, and no highly toxic chemicals. The only basin even under study is Sabinas-Burro-Picachos, which runs between Coahuila and Tamaulipas.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico Had the Lowest Energy Inflation in the Entire OECD</u>

In August, fuel prices in Mexico rose just 0.9% year on year. The average across the OECD's 38 member countries was 13.6%. The gap comes from Hacienda's fuel subsidies on gasoline and diesel, which have absorbed the international price spike instead of passing it on at the pump. Headline inflation in Mexico stood at 3.26% in August, while the OECD average climbed to 4.3%.

📸 Inauguration of the Teletón Rehabilitation and Inclusion Center — Colima, Colima, Oct 6, 2026

🇲🇽✊ "Our Constitution obliges the State to the rehabilitation of people with a permanent disability." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, opening of the Teletón Rehabilitation and Inclusion Center, Colima, Oct 6, 2026 Since December 2024, Article 4 of the Constitution carries two obligations: a scholarship for every person with a permanent disability, and the State's duty to guarantee their rehabilitation, with priority for those under 18. The amendment passed with the support of every political party. The federal government pays the scholarship from age 0 to 29, most states cover 30 to 65, and the universal pension takes over from there. Since 2025 the government has paid Teletón the scholarships of the children it treats.

text: 🇲🇽✊ "A space that was once associated with the exercise of power is today destined for the exercise of rights." — Indira Vizcaíno, Governor of Colima, Teletón center opening, Oct 6, 2026 The new Teletón rehabilitation center stands on land that was part of the "Governor's Hacienda" from the late 19th century. Griselda Álvarez, the first woman governor in Mexico's history, turned it into a public park. The center will treat about 700 children and teenagers a year with motor disabilities and autism, from every municipality in Colima and parts of Jalisco and Michoacán. It was built in 228 days. "This collaboration does not replace the responsibilities of public institutions. It complements them."
